Concrete findings:

1. **P2 — Failed history reads qualify for the unchanged-input cache shortcut.**  
   [file_view/mod.rs:150](/home/jonas/.t3/worktrees/gitcraft/t3-572729bb/src/repo/file_view/mod.rs:150) checks `view.history.is_some()`, which includes `Some(Err(_))`. Meanwhile, [line_history.rs:55](/home/jonas/.t3/worktrees/gitcraft/t3-572729bb/src/repo/file_view/line_history.rs:55) retains the successful input key even when the subsequent log fails. After a transient Git/I/O failure, later successful status probes with the same key skip the log indefinitely until a full reload or reopening. Previously, status updates invalidated that failure. **Remedy:** require `Some(Ok(_))` for the shortcut, or cache inputs only alongside successful history.

2. **P2 — The new key can combine a mapping from one HEAD with another HEAD’s object ID.**  
   [line_log.rs:46](/home/jonas/.t3/worktrees/gitcraft/t3-572729bb/src/git/line_log.rs:46) calls `committed_range`, whose rename lookup and diff independently read symbolic `HEAD`; only afterward does the key resolve `HEAD` to an OID. A concurrent commit or checkout between those commands can yield `(new_oid, old_path, old_range)`. The loader then explicitly runs history against that mismatched tuple, producing incorrect history or a missing-path/range error. Request generations cannot detect this inconsistency inside a single worker. This carries forward the mapper’s existing snapshot-coherency weakness into the new cache key. **Remedy:** resolve HEAD first and pass that immutable OID through both rename discovery and range mapping, then use it for the log.

Source tracing otherwise supports unchanged successful inputs skipping the expensive log, changed mapped path/range/OID triggering refresh, and newer probe IDs rejecting older probe replies. View generations protect refreshes, changed selections, and identical reopenings. Full reload still unconditionally invalidates mutable views; explicit probe errors request a normal reread.

**P2 — Failed line-history reads become cached across status refreshes.** In [file_view/mod.rs:150](/home/jonas/.t3/worktrees/gitcraft/t3-572729bb/src/repo/file_view/mod.rs:150), the unchanged-input shortcut accepts `view.history.is_some()`, including `Some(Err(_))`. Meanwhile, [line_history.rs:62](/home/jonas/.t3/worktrees/gitcraft/t3-572729bb/src/repo/file_view/line_history.rs:62) saves successfully resolved inputs even when the subsequent history read fails.

Reachable sequence: input resolution succeeds; `git log -L` fails—for example, because a remote connection drops; connectivity recovers; another status refresh resolves the same inputs. The shortcut retains the error instead of retrying. Previously, status refresh invalidated that failure.

**Remedy:** reuse unchanged inputs only when history contains a successful result, using `matches!(&view.history, Some(Ok(_)))`. Add a regression covering successful key resolution, failed history, and an unchanged-key refresh that retries.
